patch.objective: Process improvement with Lean, Six Sigma and process mining of system event logs
secondaryObjectives: Evaluating health informatics solutions and their impact

sources.cite: AMIA Accreditation Committee, foundational domains for master's-level health informatics education (CAHIIM HI master's curriculum requirements PDF)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. F7 integrates business and information sciences into implementing and evaluating solutions; the MSHI course places Lean and Six Sigma process improvement there. The case is a food line, not a hospital: the Six Sigma decision it teaches (choose the control chart that fits the data, find the special cause before acting, never tamper with a stable process) is the one a health informatics process improvement project makes with turnaround times or wait times.

sources.cite: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 6.3.2.1 Shewhart X-bar and R and S Control Charts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: X-bar chart UCL = x-double-bar + A2 R-bar, center line x-double-bar, LCL = x-double-bar - A2 R-bar; R chart UCL = R-bar D4, center line R-bar, LCL = R-bar D3; A2 = 3/(d2 sqrt(n)). The factor values used (A2 = 0.577, D3 = 0, D4 = 2.114 for subgroups of 5) are the standard table values and were not on the fetched page; the limits in the case (R-bar 3.1 g: 500.2 to 503.8 g, R up to 6.55 g) are computed from them.

sources.cite: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 6.3.2 What are Variables Control Charts? (WECO rules)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: the WECO rules, among them '8 Consecutive Points on This Side of Control Line' and '2 Out of the Last 3 Points Below -2 Sigma'; for a point outside the control limits 'we conclude the process has shifted and is unstable'. The page gives no corrective procedure; finding and removing the cause before adjusting is the case's teaching, consistent with the objective.

sources.cite: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 6.3.3.2 Proportions Control Charts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: p 'is the fraction defective in a lot or population'; 'the control chart for proportion or fraction nonconforming ... is called the p-chart'. The p-chart limits in the case (p-bar 0.07, n = 5, UCL 0.41) are computed with the usual three-sigma binomial form, which was not on the fetched text.
